pr_comments:
Hello, thank you!

This is not right. We want to update the stats, not having an extra metric.

Plus, we want two stats:

Total touched samples and maximum touched samples at a certain point.

I have imagined adding in stats:

(pseudocode)
```
stats.Observe(samples){
 if samples > max {
  max = samples
 }
 total += samples
}
```
@roidelapluie I think the stats are being sent as metrics. That's why when we have an extra parameter `stats=true`, we send timings which are stats as a response. Please correct me if I am wrong.

The stats are a separate bag of metadata kept in https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/45fbed94d6ee17840254e78cfc421ab1db78f734/promql/engine.go#L145, not normal Prometheus metrics.

Currently those stats living in https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/master/util/stats/query_stats.go only support timers. The whole type would have to be extended / refactored / renamed to support simple non-duration stats fields as well.

> Maybe evaluatorCount is not what we want.

Yeah, that's a property of the query not the execution of it.

@brian-brazil , since samples are fetched only in vector selectors, should peakSamples be calculated only as the sum of all the samples across all the vectorselectors? Otherwise, it will be a repeat calculation and the result might be wrong.
@brian-brazil I have updated the logic as per my current understanding, keeping in mind to avoid repeated samples in peak sample calculations as well.

The current implementation is on the following:

Total samples: They represent the number of samples involved in the calculation of the root AST node (only). This is because the user expects the total samples to represent the number of samples that have been considered for his query as the final result.

Peak samples: Samples that are brought to memory from tsdb prior to performing any calculation. Since, fetching is only at vector selectors, it is the sum of samples of all vector selector nodes in any expression.

> They represent the number of samples involved in the calculation of the root AST node (only). 

That's not really of much use, the root node is generally the cheapest node to calculate. The useful number is how many samples all nodes touch.

> Peak samples: Samples that are brought to memory from tsdb prior to performing any calculation. 

That's not peak samples in memory, that's samples loaded from the tsdb. Peak samples is basically the highest value currentSamples hits.
@brian-brazil updated as per what you mentioned.

Peak looks better, but you've missed a few other places where it needs to be checked.

The total is a mix of input and output, it should only be the inputs.

issue_context.title: PromQL: add "involved samples" for query stats
issue_context.body:
## Proposal

Prometheus will record `timings stats` for every query, such as `evalTotalTime `, `resultSortTime` now. It need more stats to evaluate query performance.

**What is we need?**

Expose stats "involved sample" as a query stats, i.e. `currentSamples` https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/0eb34299dad0ab997bc9d9363a06d6ea6eb45dad/promql/engine.go#L785 

**Why is it important?**

The `timings stats` is an unstable metric, which may be affected by hardware, query queue, etc., especially it's a random number. Sometimes we wanna evaluate whether query was bad or good, using `timings stats` is not a good idea.

However, `currentSamples` is stable and reliable which precisely records how many samples a query travelled. It also reflect how much computation resource consumed, such as memory or cpu.
comments: Current samples is a guage, not a counter, so is updated throughout the query. What you'd want is peak samples.

Gauge is what i want. I wanna track a promql explain plan like sql.

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/prometheus-users/kZ2DvZnYHUA
I am taking this up. Thank you.
I think we want: the number of series, the number of samples and the peak number of samples. Thanks.
@roidelapluie not sure about the `evaluatorsCount`, but rest all looks :+1: . Moving ahead with this as of now.
At bug-scrub: we believe this was addressed by #10369.

review_comments:
This feels low for a subquery, what does a more complex subquery produce?

To test this properly we should also add in some aggregators, binary operators, and functions on instant vectors.

Ran instant query (after a min of prometheus start) for the following:

`go_goroutines[5m:10s]` => 13 (verified via console)

`go_goroutines[5m:10s]` => 201 (verified via console)
@brian-brazil does it look satisfactory now, after adding more test cases?
There still needs to be a complex subquery.
This deserves a comment, that's we're doing a single count of the overall output.
This comment reads oddly. Something like Include output samples in overall samples touched would be clearer.
Can we get a test for metric + 1 too?
This is wrong, it can't be less than the TotalSamples for metric[10s:1s]

I think thats because in case of vector selectors, we only calculate during the output. But, here just after evaluating the VS, we go to subquery and then prom function, and hence the samples are selectively chosen based on timestamps, thus reducing the total samples. But, since peak is carried over, so it remains good.
So, should we consider adding the samples from `len(res.(Matrix))` (pseudo code) to `totalSamples` after evaluating a subquery?
Yes, and ensure than any TotalSamples from that query is also included.
This isn't right, as this is only how many samples we just processed - not how many are currently held in memory.

That is what the total samples is for: to catch and store the total count of samples while querying.

Could you explain in detail what you meant or expected?
The PeakSamples should be the highest amount of samples we had in memory at once.

Got it. However, I wanted to know that does this issue aims to count the number of samples the query is considering while evaluation (which is similar to the number of points) or does this aims for the number of samples it had to scan (including the ones that are skipped while appending points).
I'd do it as every input point processed. At the PromQL level, we don't know anything about skipped samples.

> I'd do it as every input point processed

Assuming this as when every point is being appended to the vector.

> PeakSamples should be the highest amount of samples we had in memory at once

I hope this means the total number of samples fetched from tsdb into memory for a particular node. Is that correct?

> Assuming this as when every point is being appended to the vector.

Before it's passed in I'd say. A rate 1d is more expensive to calculate than a 1h.

> I hope this means the total number of samples fetched from tsdb into memory. Is that correct?

That's part of it, it's also all the outputs that are currently in memory.

> That's part of it, it's also all the outputs that are currently in memory.

That means the values of PeakSamples is monotonicaly increasing?
It's a peak value, so it can't go down within a query.
Okay got it. Can you differentiate the between of `totalSamples` vs `peakSamples` as per what you think, so that it clears all my doubts? I will make the changes right away.
They're very different things. One is data processed, one is peak memory.
If that's the case, for **peak memory**, why not have a function in SeriesIterator as `SamplesCount()` that returns the number of samples across all the series?
That's not peak samples, that's input samples.

> input samples

Aren't the input samples the ones that contribute to memory usage?

Yes, but they're generally a pretty small part of it as how we evaluate range vector functions is optimised so we only need to hold the range for one series in memory at a time. It's the intermediate results that are more the issue.
